findings.title: Conditional passkey UI is no longer set up on the username-less login page
findings.body: The guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns false whenever no user is set, because the helper at line 161 requires `user != null`. Before this PR, passkey setup ran when `context.getUser() == null` (the first login page). This change inverts that: `fillContextForm` now runs only when a user is already set, which is the re-authentication case. The same inverted guard appears in `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137. Consequence: on the initial login page the conditional-UI attributes are never set, so the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the passkey form disappear, discoverable-key auto-login stops working, and invalid-username error pages lose passkeys. Existing and new tests that assert the first-page autocomplete and webauth form (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey, passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, and the first-page checks in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) would fail. Passkeys should be gated only on passkeys being enabled; the re-authentication case should be added on top of the existing null-user behavior, not replace it.

findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments, but the only definition in UsernamePasswordForm (the superclass) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and no zero-argument overload exists in the class hierarchy shown. The services module will fail to compile. The call was probably meant to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: NoSuchElementException import is now unused
findings.body: The two `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` calls were replaced in this PR, and no other use of `NoSuchElementException` remains in this file. The import is left dangling, which a checkstyle unused-import check would flag.

findings.title: PasswordCredentialModel import added but never used
findings.body: This PR adds the `org.keycloak.models.credential.PasswordCredentialModel` import, but nothing in the file references it. Unused imports are lint failures in this codebase.

findings.title: Negative webauthn-form check swallows every exception, so it can pass vacuously
findings.body: The check wraps `findElement` in `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. Any exception, including a WebDriverException from a broken page or session, makes the assertion pass. The same pattern is repeated at line 315. The rest of the suite uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` or `driver.findElements(...).isEmpty()`, which would catch only the intended condition.

findings.title: Test comment and name misattribute why passkeys are hidden
findings.body: The comment says passkeys are not shown 'as this user does not have passkey', and the test is named reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey. But the test actually disables passkeys at realm level (line 282), and the production check is realm-only (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled checks the realm policy, not the user's credentials). As a result, no test covers a passkeys-enabled realm with a user who has no passkey, which is the case the name and comment describe.

findings.title: SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS stays true for conditional UI when a user is set
findings.body: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides only shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to suppress the authenticator list. shouldDisplayAuthenticators (lines 147-149) still returns context.getUser() != null, so during re-authentication fillContextForm sets SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true while ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS is never set. Whether the template then renders an empty list or fails depends on the webauthn FTL, which is not in this diff. The override looks incomplete, and the template behavior should be checked.
